title: Can NRCH swimmers divide if the chemostat lattice is given turnover: a per-swimmer maintenance cost (deaths) or a slowly rising feed, so that the lattice spacing must be re-established by fission?
summary: NRCH from noise gives self-propelled polar droplets (established SIM, 20261025T0840-c08-nrch-swimmers). Without a chemostat they split often but daughters dissolve or fuse (7 of 715 splits persistent, 20261025T1017). A strong chemostat (u(phi_t+10) ~ 0.01-0.015) locks them into a traveling crystal of identical swimmers whose number is set by the lattice spacing and then never changes (20261025T1054, 20261025T1114). Hypothesis: if swimmers are removed (an extensive maintenance cost that kills small or slow swimmers, or random whole-body deaths as in ad5) or the supply ramps up slowly, the lattice must refill by fission of its members, giving persistent splits with daughters spread apart by the chemostat's repulsion. Experiment for one loop: the parent world.py at u=1.5e-3, phi0=-0.4 on 192^2; arm A: ramp phi_t from -0.4 to -0.3 over t=3000-9000; arm B: every 500 t erase one random swimmer (whole body, matter removed); measure persistent splits and generations after t=4000 against the frozen u-only lattice, 2 seeds.
experiment: nrch world.py (c08) at u=1.5e-3, phi0=-0.4; ramp phi_t -0.4 -> -0.3 over t=3000-9000 (arm A) or remove one random swimmer every 500 t (arm B); labkit --spf 500 --lineage-k 40, T=12000, seeds 0 1; compare persistent splits after t=4000 with the unperturbed lattice
